expectations.text: Diagnoses the user's passive-consumption / watch-videos-feels-like-learning pattern explicitly
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis #1 states 'You're consuming way more than you're producing... these feel like learning, but they're passive.' and frames the whole response around the consume-vs-produce distinction.

expectations.text: Names the 'illusion of comprehension' / recognition-vs-recall distinction (following along is not knowing)
expectations.evidence: Explicitly calls it 'the illusion of comprehension' in the intro and spells out 'That's recognition, not recall. Recognition is about 10x easier than recall, and only recall generalizes...'

expectations.text: Explains why Duolingo / YouTube videos produce felt progress without transferable skill
expectations.evidence: 'Duolingo tells you you're doing great because you tapped the right tile from a set of four...' and 'watching a YouTuber play Chopin teaches you nothing about *your* hands doing it.'

expectations.text: Diagnoses attempting an advanced target (Chopin piece) without prerequisite/foundational skill
expectations.evidence: 'A Chopin piece is not a starting skill — it's an *encompassing* skill that assumes hand independence, fluency reading both clefs, basic scale patterns, dynamics, pedaling, and probably 50 more things.'

expectations.text: Includes a concrete daily session structure with time allocations
expectations.evidence: Provides 'The daily session shape (30 min is enough)' with specific time blocks: 0-7 min spaced retrieval, 7-22 active production, 22-27 interleaved practice, 27-30 self-check, plus domain-specific breakdowns for Spanish and piano.

expectations.text: Prescribes high active-production to passive-intake ratio (e.g., 3:1 or stated numerically)
expectations.evidence: 'you should be producing... at least 3x as much time as you spend consuming' and rule #3: 'active production, in a ratio of ~3:1 over consumption.'

expectations.text: Includes spaced / distributed review of previously-learned material
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis #4 covers memory decay with expanding intervals (1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, a month); daily session includes a 'Spaced retrieval warm-up' block; Spanish plan uses Anki reviews.

expectations.text: Includes retrieval-based practice or self-testing without looking at notes
expectations.evidence: 'Pull old stuff from memory, no notes. Check.' and the Spanish plan: 'Stop and summarize out loud what you just heard, without replaying. This is forced retrieval...'

expectations.text: Names specific resources or tool types (e.g., Anki, tutor/language partner, a specific course)
expectations.evidence: Names Anki, iTalki tutor, Dreaming Spanish, Language Transfer, Alfred's Adult All-in-One, Faber Adult Piano Adventures, Hanon exercises, Bach 2-part invention #1 in C, Chopin prelude #7 in A.

expectations.text: Warns that the right approach will feel harder/slower than what they were doing before (desirable difficulty)
expectations.evidence: A whole section 'What to expect' warns 'The new method is going to feel worse than what you were doing before' and explicitly names 'desirable difficulty' as the concept.

expectations.text: Explicitly recommends focusing on ONE skill rather than multiple simultaneously
expectations.evidence: The 'Pick one' section says 'Don't restart both Spanish and piano at once. Pick ONE and do it for 3 months with this system before adding anything.'

expectations.text: Provides a concrete starting template or plan (not just principles) they can act on
expectations.evidence: Provides full templates for Spanish (daily Anki + production + Dreaming Spanish schedule, weekly iTalki) and piano (daily warm-up, deliberate practice, interleaving, weekly recording, monthly lesson) with specific goals and timelines.
